headline.text: The Ballad of the Nine-Man Bees

lines.text: A penalty for Liverpool
was cancelled by the screen;
two minutes on, Keane Lewis-Potter
rose up and headed clean.
It came from Igor Thiago's cross
and found the topmost nook:
one–nil, and all the Gtech roared;
the Reds could only look.
But deep in first-half added time
Yarmoliuk lost his head:
he aimed it, grappling, at Jacquet,
and VAR turned it red.
With ten men left, the Bees held firm
until the sixty-second,
when Wirtz sent Muñoz down the right,
and one–one, the scoreboard reckoned.
Mac Allister swung in a cross,
and Barcola headed back,
and Isak, fresh from injury,
struck home to end the attack.
Then, in the last of added time,
Janelt pulled Ngumoha back;
a second yellow sent him off,
and the Bees were nine, alack.
So sing it soft in Brentford town
and loud on Merseyside:
two goals to one to Liverpool,
who came from behind and turned the tide.

facts.text: Final score: Brentford 1–2 Liverpool, at the Gtech Community Stadium on Saturday 17 October 2026, kick-off 3pm.
44': Keane Lewis-Potter headed Igor Thiago's cross into the top right corner. Brentford 1, Liverpool 0. Lewis-Potter is among the smallest players on the pitch.

Two minutes before the opener, referee John Brooks gave Liverpool a penalty for a trip by Dango Ouattara on Alexis Mac Allister, then overturned it after a VAR review showed Ouattara touched the ball.
45+8': Yehor Yarmoliuk (Brentford) was sent off for violent conduct.
VAR spotted Yarmoliuk aiming a headbutting action at Jérémy Jacquet as they grappled at a corner.
62': Víctor Muñoz, sent racing down the right by Florian Wirtz on a fast break, cut inside and scored with a left-footed shot into the bottom corner. Brentford 1, Liverpool 1.
70': Alexander Isak scored from very close range with his left foot after Bradley Barcola headed the ball back to him. Brentford 1, Liverpool 2.
The winner began with a deep cross from Alexis Mac Allister towards the far post.
Isak had missed Liverpool's previous two matches through injury; the winner was his fifth goal of the season.
90+2': Vitaly Janelt (Brentford) was sent off for a second yellow card, for pulling back Rio Ngumoha. Brentford finished with nine men.
Bradley Barcola, a £123m signing, had a free run on goal after a Janelt mistake, tried to chip goalkeeper Caoimhín Kelleher and stabbed the ball wide.
Home fans behind the goal sang "what a waste of money" after Barcola's miss.
Dominik Szoboszlai went off injured after 32 minutes.
Liverpool had 59.9% of possession and 21 shots to Brentford's 10.

headline.text: Sonnet for a Head Too Rash

lines.text: Two minutes after VAR had wiped a kick,
Keane Lewis-Potter, smallest on the green,
rose up to Thiago's cross and nodded quick
into the topmost corner, sharp and clean.
But rashness waits where added minutes run:
at a corner Yarmoliuk dipped his head
at Jacquet; and the screen, when all was done,
showed Brooks the deed, and Brooks showed him the red.
Then ten held on, till Wirtz sent Muñoz clear,
whose left foot found the corner, low and true;
and Isak, two games missed, was waiting near
to turn in Barcola's header: one, then two.
Then Janelt's second yellow made them nine:
two goals to one, the Reds had crossed the line.

headline.text: The Battle of the Gtech: A Heroi-Comical Poem

lines.text: What dire offence from grappling corners springs,
what mighty wars are waged on little things,
I sing, O Muse: of Bees that held the hive,
and Reds that came to Brentford, keen to thrive.
First Fate, in VAR's all-seeing guise,
denied the Reds a penalty, their prize;
then Thiago crossed, and little Lewis-Potter
headed it home; the Gtech could not be hotter.
One goal to none! But pride before a fall:
in added time, amid the corner's brawl,
Yarmoliuk bent his brow at Jacquet's face;
the screen saw all, and red was his disgrace.
Ten Bees remained. The Reds, with greater share
of ball and shots, besieged them everywhere,
till Wirtz, the schemer, sent Muñoz flying wide,
whose left foot found the corner's lower side.
Mac Allister's deep cross, by Barcola returned,
found Isak, mended, and the tables turned.
Last, Janelt held back Ngumoha, and was sent
to join his fellow exile in lament.
So ends the tale; let Brentford weep in rhyme:
two goals to one, the Reds, in their own time.

lines.text: Keane Lewis-Potter, though small,
outjumped every Red for the ball;
from Igor's high cross
he showed who was boss,
and the Bees were one up, standing tall.
Then Yarmoliuk, hot in the head,
leaned in at poor Jacquet instead;
the screen took a look,
and Brooks, by the book,
showed a card that was terribly red.
Muñoz equalised with his left,
then Isak, back fit, scored with heft;
when Janelt saw red
all the Bees' hopes had fled:
two–one to the Reds, Bees bereft.

headline.text: Hey Diddle Diddle, the Bees in the Middle

lines.text: Hey diddle diddle, a cross to the middle,
and Lewis-Potter, the size of a fiddle,
rose up and headed it into the top,
and the Bees went one up with a hippity-hop.
Yarmoliuk, Yarmoliuk, what did you do?
You aimed your head at Jacquet, and the screen saw it too!
Red went the card, and off went the Bee,
and ten little Bees were left: one, two, three…
Wirtz sent Muñoz running down the right;
left foot, low corner: one–one, and the hive took fright.
Then Barcola's header found Isak, mended and spry,
who knocked it in close as the Bees wondered why.
Janelt held Ngumoha, and yellow came twice,
so nine little Bees found the Gtech not so nice;
two goals to one, sing it high, sing it low,
and that's how the Reds beat the Bees, you know.
